action.en: Research exact FE/BE revisions, manifests, entrypoints, DI, API handlers, data stores, jobs, deploy topology and tests. Trace each network hop from caller symbol through URL/config resolution, proxy/ingress wiring, receiving handler and deployment owner; record synchronous, async and in-process edges separately. Names and comments are clues, not endpoint proof. Keep observed and desired routing separate and block contradictory boundary decisions. Resolve the execution profile and actual tool availability before selecting instruments; this does not switch the model/runtime or spawn workers.

Map accepted business flow and AC IDs to responsible services and authoritative data writers. Draw the logical request/response and asynchronous event sequence in ordered flow rows, including trust boundaries; never assume a class is an independently deployed service. Write ordered serviceCalls with caller/callee service IDs, caller/receiver source refs, operation, endpoint binding, credentials/trust boundary, data classification, timeout/retry and evidence status. Verify response path and downstream side effects. Unobserved deployment/runtime facts remain unknown.

Choose the smallest design satisfying accepted invariants and actual constraints. Challenge one coherent proposal with a materially simpler alternative, trade-offs and a reasoned decision. Select concerns from real business risks, data value, scale, trust boundaries and operating model, not a universal technology checklist. Evaluate named patterns only when relevant; patternDecisions may be empty. An adopted Saga/CQRS/outbox must describe actual mechanisms, not labels or handler filenames. Specify applicable transaction, idempotency, ordering, timeout, concurrency and recovery behavior; never invent numeric targets or unresolved product policy.

Write codeImpacts with exact repository/path/symbol, observed/proposed identity, direct/transitive relation, change/preserve/review decision, reason, caller chain, tests and protected paths. Write serviceImpacts with deployable owner, inbound/outbound consumers, stores/events, compatibility, rollout/rollback and observability; explain unaffected boundaries. Map every selected pattern and service call back to exact source symbols, data/event schemas, deployment/config owners and protected paths. Do not route traffic to a different service merely because its repository contains a matching resolver.

Review each trust boundary: authentication, object/tenant authorization, validation, credential custody, sensitive logs, external provider/AI input, replay and resource abuse where relevant. Link threat, server-side control owner, code/service impact and positive/negative AC. Record residual risks and decision owner without claiming a security audit ran. Add a threat model per trust boundary: assets, entry points, attacker capability, exploit path, impact, prevention/detection, control owner and negative acceptance. Assess object/function/property authorization, tenant isolation, token issuer/audience/scope and forwarding, SSRF/redirect/DNS/egress, injection, webhook authenticity/replay, resource/AI cost abuse, sensitive transcripts/logs and dependency risks when applicable. Mark non-applicability with evidence; unresolved high-impact risks need a decision owner and block acceptance.

Produce implementation ceilings, protected paths, dependencies and required checks from actual repository scripts/CI. Lint, typecheck, tests/coverage, build and Sonar execute inside FE/BE implement; this op specifies them only. Bind rollout/migration/cleanup plans without executing them. Preserve business expected results unchanged. Design failure-injection tests for wrong service target, unauthorized forwarding, stale reads, duplicate/out-of-order messages, crash after commit before publish, compensation failure and retry exhaustion as applicable; implementations run them. Author canonical user journeys and journeyCoverage links to flow/AC IDs using the shared journey contract; preserve accepted journeys unchanged in architecture. Do not convert internal service hops into UI actions. Browser-free scope may use an empty array only when no UAT acceptance is assigned. Record architectureReview with context-selected concerns linked to requirements, sources, concrete trigger/impact/control/owner/acceptance scenarios, decisions, residual risks and evidence limitations. Examine persistence, connections, failure domains, capacity, security, HA, backup/restore, provider or total-infrastructure loss only to the depth their consequences require in this scope. Where durable customer state is in scope, identify authoritative versus rebuildable data, all stores/volumes/config/Secrets/keys, consistency point, independent backup custody, recovery prerequisites/order and verification. Never claim every possible edge case is covered or a recovery drill ran from design prose. Current external production practices need primary sources and an explicit applicability argument.

Validate target ownership, request/data/credential paths, contracts and applicable failure controls against accepted Business and actual sources. Separate proposed design from observations and implementation gaps. Require accepted decisions for material concerns and residual risks before passing design review. Omit unnecessary Saga/CQRS designs; validate concrete mechanisms when selected. Preserve accepted SRS requirements/flows/AC and user journeys, with explicit business leaf dependencies. Architecture done means reviewed design only, never implementation, security audit, HA or executed restore proof.

action.en: Bind the exact operation/AC set and inspect existing code plus sibling conventions, including DI/module registration and every relevant caller. Reuse already conforming behavior. Own preparation through delivery: inspect readiness and reproduce the requested defect when applicable, partition the selected work into cohesive changes and check callers before editing. Resolve repository-local dependencies and bounded development runtime needs under the existing scope. Shared library changes belong to the actual FE or BE package owner: include owner tests, packaging/export compatibility and selected consumer integration proof in this same implementation; never publish a package implicitly. Keep shared paths exclusive and report a missing required external authority rather than inventing a helper. Resolve the execution profile and actual tool availability before selecting instruments; this does not switch the model/runtime or spawn workers.
Implement transport, validation, permission checks, use-case logic and persistence inside the declared ownership. Enforce denials before unauthorized side effects; do not invent fallback behavior.
Implement declared transaction, retry/idempotency, concurrency, error identity and read-time revalidation. Migrations are source only; applying them remotely is not included.

Add or repair scoped unit tests, then execute the repository's backend unit gate and retain command, exit code, counts and sanitized output. Next execute the relevant backend E2E gate against the actual backend contract, persistence and authorization boundary; browser/frontend UAT is not backend E2E. Positive, denial, invalid-input and applicable race/reload cases must map to the selected operations. Unit success cannot substitute for E2E, and an unavailable runner, dependency, environment or required case is blocked/not-run rather than pass. After both gates pass, run required lint, typecheck, coverage, build and Sonar checks against the same source revision. Preserve failures, repair only within the approved goal, rerun affected gates, and never delegate this responsibility to frontend or UAT.

Review the diff and verify no unrelated changes. A passing backend delivery requires scoped unit and backend E2E evidence, every applicable quality gate, the exact tested source tree, API contract, authorization/error behavior, and runtime identity when the consumer requires a runnable API. Commit only when authorized, then read back the full SHA/diff and prove the tested tree corresponds to that commit; otherwise report uncommitted or no-change honestly. A frontend support response must return codeRefs, changedPaths, apiContract, runtime, qualityEvidence and testedCommit bound to the caller request. Missing or not-run unit/E2E proof, commit mismatch, or unavailable required served runtime blocks the handoff, so frontend cannot consume it as verified backend. Never bypass hooks, push, stage unrelated files or invent proof.

Scoped unit tests and backend E2E tests both pass for each declared operation facet, including negative authorization and persistent state when promised. Compile-only, mocked-unit-only, frontend browser UAT, missing-runner or not-run output cannot certify backend behavior.

Scanner submission without the processed server result, a missing runner/token/dependency, or any not-run required gate is blocked rather than pass.
